newsitem.title: USA: UK cable TV junk bonds in U.S. still find favor.
newsitem.headline: UK cable TV junk bonds in U.S. still find favor.

text.p: U.S. junk bond investors are still fundamentally positive on the outlook for the cable industry in the United Kingdom despite a recent decision by Standard & Poor's to put four U.K. cable companies on watch for a ratings downgrade.

"On a long-term basis the fundamentals are still intact," said Eric Takaha, assistant portfolio manager at Franklin Templeton Group. "Telephony penetration rates remain favorable to what people expected and there will be consolidation plays over the next 12-18 months."

That view contrasts starkly with that of S&P, which said prospects for the sector have weakened over the medium to longer term. S&P cited concerns about mixed consumer acceptance of the cable/telephony product, slower-than -anticipated network buildouts, and pressure from competitors such as digital broadcast satellite service, BSKYB, and in the future, digital terrestrial television.
While acknowledging the validity of S&P's concerns, most U.S. investors said they were nothing new.
"Certainly we share the view that competition is increasing, but we never thought otherwise," said Alan Ginsberg, head of high-yield research and cable analyst at Smith Barney Inc.

Ginsberg said buildouts of cable networks are proceeding aggressively, pointing out that several of the companies are now EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization) positive.

"The key right now is for the companies to as swiftly as possible complete the buildouts of plant and equipment so they can shift their focus from being construction companies to being marketing and customer service companies," he said.
Ginsberg pointed out that concerns about competition in the video market are mitigated by the success that U.K. cable companies are having in attracting telephony customers.
"When will (S&P) wake up and realize that these are telephone companies? Cable will be a secondary business," said Jerry Paul, who manages $900 million in high-yield bonds for INVESCO Trust Co.

Paul pointed out that because of their success in telephony, U.K. cable companies will be attractive aquistion targets for large telecommunications companies once competitive barriers in the European telcoms market come down in 1998.
Analysts said merger and acquisition speculation has benefitted the bonds of one U.K cable company in particular, Diamond Cable Communications Plc, which has 1.22 million subscribers.

On Friday, Diamond Cable increased the size of a zero coupon bond offering to $250 million from $175 million due to strong investor demand. The deal price on the tight end of price talk at 10.75 percent.
Despite such positive sentiment, analysts noted that S&P's decision has contributed to recent spread-widening in the U.K. cable sector.
Analysts said price weakness caused International CableTel Inc's offering of $400 million in junk bonds and preferred stock to price near the wide end of price talk two weeks ago.

Oren Cohen, high-yield cable analyst at Bear, Stearns & Co Inc, said that if S&P decided to downgrade one or all of the companies, cross-over investors could head for the doors, causing spreads to widen even further.

Cohen said he is positive on the industry's long-term outlook. Still, he expected the rating agency to downgrade at least one of the four companies on watch: TeleWest Communications Plc, International CableTel, Diamond Cable, and Comcast UK Cable Partners Ltd.
He said TeleWest and International CableTel may be the most vulnerable to a downgrade because S&P rates those credits higher than Moody's Investors Service Inc.
TeleWest is rated B1/BB and International CableTel is rated B3/B.
But further problems in the sector could be considered opportunities by some investors.
INVESCO's Paul said, "If (S&P) knocks them down and spreads widen, I will buy more of them."
